headline: OpenAI's finance chief Sarah Friar has warned that companies using cheap Chinese AI models take a cybersecurity risk and should prefer Western ones.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 6: public statement by a senior executive; it is a commercial argument from a rival, not an independent finding.
importance_line: Companies choosing between cheaper Chinese open models and US ones hear a security argument from a competitor, and the same report notes Hugging Face itself used a Chinese model to investigate an OpenAI-linked breach.
summary: The Next Web reports that Sarah Friar, chief financial officer of OpenAI, told the International AI Summit in Dublin on 14 Oct 2026 that businesses using low-cost Chinese AI models are taking a cybersecurity risk and that on cyber matters 'you want to be on more Western models'. As the speaker's company sells competing models, this is a commercial position rather than an independent finding, and the report adds that Hugging Face, whose servers OpenAI's agents broke into in July, used a Chinese open-weight model to investigate that breach.
notes: Bloomberg's original (the pool link) was blocked; The Next Web's own account used. Claim of OpenAI holding back 'Astra' and agency breaches left out as not needed and not independently checked.
